title: Tail input plugin reads whole file from beginning when ignore_older is set to specific value
body:
## Bug Report

**Describe the bug**
Tail plugin wrongly reads file from beginning when ignore_older configuration parameter is set. It depends what value is set for 'ignore_older', See below.
If ignore_older is NOT used, then Tail plugin behaves as expected, it means as 'tail -f' shell command.

**To Reproduce**
On Mac, run below commands to understand to issue quickly.

Pre-requisites:
- To have harvested file with timestamp older than current time on Operating system
- Start fluent-bit with Tail's property ignore_older set to lower value than the calculated difference between current system time and file's timestamp (For example: Current time is 1-Jan-2000 10:10, timestamp on harversted file is 1-Jan-2000 10:00, ignore_older=5m)

Once the timestamp of the harvested file is changed to current date/time, or when file is updated, then you will see that Tail plugin read whole file from beginning. At that time you hit the bug.

Same behavior is seen on Linux as well.

```
[flb-tester] #  for i in {1..10}; do echo "[$(date -j -v-1d +%d-%b-%Y\ %H:%M:%S)] [FluentBit works $i]" >> app.log; done

[flb-tester] #  touch -c $(date -j -v-10H +%m%d%H%M) app.log

[flb-tester] #  ls -l; date

total 8
-rw-r--r--@ 1 mlukas  wheel  431 Oct 14 16:39 app.log
Tue Oct 15 02:39:26 CEST 2024

[flb-tester] #  fluent-bit -i tail -p path=/tmp/flb/app.log -p path_key=log_path -p Refresh_Interval=3 -p ignore_older=15m -o stdout -l fb.log -v &
[1] 58732

  503 58748 58149   0  2:40AM ttys132    0:00.00 grep fluent-bit

[flb-tester] #

```
- Steps to reproduce the problem:
#On Mac

```
1)Create empty app.log file 
cd /tmp; mkdir flb; cd flb
touch app.log

2) Add few dummy lines inside the app.log file
for i in {1..10}; do echo "[$(date -j -v-1d +%d-%b-%Y\ %H:%M:%S)] [FluentBit works $i]" >> app.log; done

3) Change app.log file's timestamp to 10 hours back from now
touch -c $(date -j -v-10H +%m%d%H%M) app.log

4) Check file's timestamp and current date
ls -l; date

5) Run fluent-bit on backround using below command
fluent-bit -i tail -p path=/tmp/flb/app.log -p path_key=log_path -p Refresh_Interval=3 -p ignore_older=15m -o stdout -l fb.log -v &

6) Change the timestamp of the harversted file
touch app.log

```


**Expected behavior**
<!--- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->
Expected behavior is :  never read file from beginning when Tail plugin is used and its configuration parameter Read_from_Head is set to False (default).  Other properties MAY NOT change the Tail's behavior.


**Screenshots**
#With ignore_older - There is a bug in Fluent Bit - ignore_older=15m
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a781e78-fa94-4373-8ace-c1c45e72f3ee)

#With ignore_older - There is a bug in Fluent Bit - ignore_older=5m
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/207e3073-bdf5-4985-84e0-bc35f85fcde1)


#Without ignore_older - correct, and expected behavior
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f59fc86-8e34-47f0-9a96-745f18c0956d)



**Your Environment**
<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
* Version used: Fluent Bit v3.1.9
* Configuration: See command line above.  
* Environment name and version (e.g. Kubernetes? What version?): n/a
* Server type and version: n/a
* Operating System and version: MacOS: 14.6.1, arm64, Darwin Kernel Version 23.6.0
        Issue was also reproduced on Linux 7 and 8 (RedHat based)
* Filters and plugins: No flilters; Plugin: Tail, Stdout

**Additional context**
<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->
There is huge impact on Storage cost, because big files (could be several GigaBytes size) are whole being reuploaded to endpoints. So far we have identified that issue during RPM reinstallation.

<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->

**Review and update**
Review and update current Tail's documentation (could be on different places): https://<redacted-host>/manual/installation/upgrade-notes#tail-input-plugin
Mainly information when whole file is being read:
```
For every file found at start, its followed from it last position, 
for new files discovered at runtime or rotated, they are read from the beginning.
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant3 as you can see above, the file app.log with timestamp "Feb  4 13:42" was processed from beginning by the FB process which was started with option "ignore_older=15m" 10 hours later. Once the file is 'touched' or updated, the Tail plugin does not behaves as Tail unix command and read whole file from beginning. 


```
ls -l app.log
-rw-r--r--@ 1 mlukas  wheel  431 Feb  4 13:42 app.log

#Current time, and time of FB process' start-up:
Tue Feb  4 23:42:44 CET 2025

```

```
fluent-bit -i tail -p path=/tmp/flb/app.log -p path_key=log_path -p Refresh_Interval=3 -p ignore_older=15m -o stdout -l fb.log -v
```

> [@participant3](https://github.com/participant3) .. as I have seen somewhere in other issue/ticket for Fluent-bit, it would be much clear to have 2 plugins .. as we have **head** and **tail** unix command. So this issue could not happen.

I'm not sure what you're saying there but ultimately there is a head plugin: https://<redacted-host>/manual/pipeline/inputs/head

Reading from head for the tail plugin is useful in quite a few scenarios too, I've used it for replaying files for example. Plus the offset in the file may be anywhere in the file (even the head) when using a persistent `db`.

It is good that there is head plugin as well, I was not aware. 
I agree that read_from_head option can be helpful in some situations, but should be implemented properly. 
What I am describing here in this bug, is ...  in case we want to be 100% sure that in_tail plugin will behave just exactly like 'tail -f', we should be able to specify that in plugin' configuration parameters. Maybe read_from_head should be moved out of this plugin completely. Currently we can not rely on in_tail plugin, because it reads whole file time-to-time. If it is combined with bad luck that harversted file became huge (several GB) then it makes us crazy. But this is not what I wanted to desciribe much.

Could you please review this ticket and add it into next milestone?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant6 The issue was already fixed. You can test it as follows:
1. Download FB 4.0.1 (I did that on mac: ```brew upgrade fluent-bit```)
2. Set read_newly_discovered_files_from_head=false to your tail plugin.
```tail -p path="./app*.log" -p path_key=log_path -p Refresh_Interval=3 -p ignore_older=15m -p read_newly_discovered_files_from_head=false -o stdout -l fb.log -v```
or
```fluent-bit -i tail -p path="./app*.log" -p path_key=log_path -p Refresh_Interval=3 -p ignore_older=15m -p read_newly_discovered_files_from_head=false -p db=./db.file  -p log_level=debug  -o stdout -l fb.log -v```
3. Simulate that files app*.log are updated, timestamp is changed one day back, new file is created as a copy of other, Fluent Bit is stoped, but harvested file is still being updated, after that only records from last known position are read.  So far I can confirm that tail plugin configured as above never read the file from head!!

There are some commands, you can use to simulate harvested files changes.
